note: jwt_auth_issuer exposes the jwt/token endpoint (route jwt_auth_issuer.jwt_auth_issuer_controller_generateToken, _user_is_logged_in) that mints a signed JWT for the current user, adds the drupal.uid claim via a GENERATE-event subscriber, and can attach a token to the user-login response. Its only setting is the boolean jwt_auth_issuer.config -> jwt_in_login_response (config/install default true). Medium/hard cases are grounded in that real config object (never jwt.config): mediums read the live value after setup forces it false/true; hards toggle it and verify the strict boolean value.

evals.prompt: With the Drupal jwt_auth_issuer module enabled, how does a logged-in user obtain a JWT for their account?
evals.expected_output: Request the jwt/token route (jwt_auth_issuer.jwt_auth_issuer_controller_generateToken), which requires a logged-in user (auth: jwt_auth/basic_auth/cookie) and returns a signed JWT. In code, JwtAuth::generateToken() does the same.

evals.prompt: What does the jwt_auth_issuer module's jwt_in_login_response setting control, and what is its shipped default?
evals.expected_output: jwt_auth_issuer.config -> jwt_in_login_response (boolean, default true) controls whether a jwt token is added to the JSON body of the core user-login response (via JwtLoginSubscriber). It is toggled by a checkbox on the base module's config form.

evals.prompt: When jwt_auth_issuer mints a token, what makes that token identify the issuing user to jwt_auth_consumer?
evals.expected_output: Its JwtAuthIssuerSubscriber listens on JwtAuthEvents::GENERATE and stamps the current user's id as the nested drupal.uid claim, which jwt_auth_consumer then reads to resolve the account.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, is jwt_auth_issuer currently configured to include a JWT in the user login response? Inspect the live configuration and answer.
evals.expected_output: No — jwt_auth_issuer.config jwt_in_login_response is FALSE on this site, so no token is added to the login response. Read it with `drush cget jwt_auth_issuer.config jwt_in_login_response`.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, will a successful user login response include a JWT token? Inspect the live jwt_auth_issuer configuration and answer.
evals.expected_output: Yes — jwt_auth_issuer.config jwt_in_login_response is TRUE, so JwtLoginSubscriber adds a jwt token to the login response. Read it with `drush cget jwt_auth_issuer.config jwt_in_login_response`.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site currently adds a JWT to the user login response, and we want to stop that. Configure jwt_auth_issuer so that no JWT is included in the login response. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set jwt_auth_issuer.config jwt_in_login_response to FALSE (e.g. `drush cset jwt_auth_issuer.config jwt_in_login_response 0`, or untick the checkbox on /admin/config/system/jwt). Verify passes when the value is strictly FALSE.

evals.prompt: A decoupled client needs the login endpoint to return a JWT so it can immediately authenticate follow-up requests. Configure jwt_auth_issuer so a JWT is included in the user login response. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set jwt_auth_issuer.config jwt_in_login_response to TRUE (e.g. `drush cset jwt_auth_issuer.config jwt_in_login_response 1`, or tick the checkbox on /admin/config/system/jwt). Verify passes when the value is strictly TRUE.
